summary:
Orbit is an interactive educational website. It aims to teach young students about rovers sent to Mars and the Moon, particularly Spirit & Opportunity on Mars, and Apollo's 15 Rover  and its lander Falcon on the Moon.
We believe this project is important because it provides an interactive experience instead of just reading a blog which might feel boring for some people. This website also uses sound effects and multiple choices that have different outcomes through the story so the user is kept engaged and interested, which enhances the educational experience. Orbit will not only explain what rovers are for young students in a fun way, but it also will preserve the legacy of the rovers sent to the Moon and Mars, even if they never came back to Earth.
details:
Orbit is an interactive educational website. It aims to teach young students about rovers sent to Mars and the Moon in the form of a game, particularly Spirit and Opportunity on Mars, and Apollo's 15 Rover and its lander Falcon on the Moon.
Each rover has a full chapter with a locked test that opens after you finish the chapter to test whether students understood the story of the rover. Each chapter uses sound effects, multiple choices each with its own outcome, animation, and finally the test to make sure the player stays engaged and doesn't get bored by the relatively long duration of the chapter.
To make this project, we used visual studio code, GitHub, and Claude. We also used LibreOffice for editing the presentation slides. The coding languages used were: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and jQuery for the starfield in the background.

We believe our project is creative because it avoids plain storytelling which might get boring. Instead, it uses interactive methods such as choices, tests, and animation to keep the user engaged.
We considered keeping the story's language relatively simple so it appeals for different audiences, especially kids and teens who are the main audience. We also considered adding sound effects so the story doesn't stay silent, and adding tests so students can test their knowledge. We also made the option to retake a test, so that you can try again and beat your best score, which we believe will help users achieve the greatest value of this experience.

The link for our project's GitHub Repo: https://github.com/sarahzoghly/SOS
